mainTopic: A נזיר in double doubt (maybe טמא, maybe a confirmed מצורע), and whether days of צרעת count toward נזירות, as a challenge to רב חסדא.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a משנה about a נזיר whose status is doubly uncertain: he may be טמא from a dead body, or he may be a confirmed מצורע. Because he must cover every possibility with separate shavings, he may eat קדשים only after sixty days, and he may drink wine and become טמא to the dead only after 120 days. The תוספתא adds that with a year-long נזירות these times become two years and four years. The גמרא uses that four-year figure against רב חסדא. If the days of צרעת counted toward נזירות, three years and thirty days would be enough. רב אשי then brings a second challenge from a ברייתא that assumes the days of confirmed צרעת (ימי חלוטו) do not count and looks for the source. A comparison to days of טומאה is rejected, and a קל וחומר from a נזיר who vowed in a graveyard proves the point instead. The ברייתא then asks how we know that the days of counting toward purification (ימי ספרו) also do not count, and it begins a logical proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sixty days for קדשים, 120 days for wine and טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source rules that this doubtful נזיר may eat קדשים after sixty days, and may drink wine and become טמא to the dead only after 120 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may eat sacrificial food after sixty days, and he may drink wine and become impure to the dead after one hundred and twenty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of quoting a משנה about a נזיר who might be טמא and might be a confirmed מצורע, which gives two waiting periods: sixty days for eating קדשים, and 120 days for drinking wine and becoming טמא to the dead. This quote sets up a challenge against רב חסדא, which comes in Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A confirmed מצורע needs two shavings before he can eat קדשים, and each shaving here can only happen thirty days apart, so it takes sixty days to be sure he has shaved twice. To finish his נזירות, he must also allow for the chance that some of those shavings counted for צרעת or for טומאה and not for his נזירות. Covering every possibility adds two more thirty-day periods, which brings the total to 120 days.

keyTerms.meaning: Eats sacrificial food, which is allowed only once he is fully טָהוֹר.
Drinks wine. A נָזִיר may do this only after his נְזִירוּת is fully finished.
Becomes טָמֵא from a dead body. This is forbidden to a נָזִיר during his נְזִירוּת.
A confirmed מְצוֹרָע, who must go through shavings as part of his purification.
The shaving of the head that ends a stage of נְזִירוּת or of purification.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate numbers here. Sixty days answers only the question of eating קדשים. Finishing the נזירות itself (wine and טומאה) takes longer, 120 days, because more doubts have to be covered.

phrases.english: He eats sacrificial food after sixty days,
phrases.notes: "He" is the נזיר who might be טמא and might be a confirmed מצורע.

phrases.english: and he drinks wine and becomes impure for the dead
after one hundred and twenty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a source the גמרא was already quoting before this section begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful טמא and doubtful מצורע נזיר may eat קדשים after 60 days, and may drink wine and become טמא to the dead after 120 days.

steps.title: For a year-long נזירות, the numbers become two and four years
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא taught on this ruling limits the 60 and 120 days to a short נזירות. With a year-long נזירות he eats קדשים after two years, and drinks wine and becomes טמא to the dead after four years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught about this: When is this said? With a short naziriteship. But with a naziriteship of a year, he eats sacrificial food after two years, and he drinks wine and becomes impure to the dead after four years.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא (the תוספתא) adds a limit to the ruling. The sixty and 120 days apply only to a regular thirty-day נזירות, and for a one-year נזירות the times become two years and four years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure of the calculation stays exactly the same. Only the length of each period changes, from thirty days to one year. So the 'two periods' needed for קדשים become two years, and the 'four periods' needed to finish the נזירות become four years.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught about it: a ברייתא that comments on the ruling just quoted.
In what case are these words said? This phrase introduces a limit on a rule.
A short נְזִירוּת, the standard thirty days.
A נְזִירוּת that a person accepted for a full year.

steps.whatToRemember: Count it in periods. Eating קדשים takes two periods, and finishing the נזירות takes four. Each period is thirty days for a regular נזירות (60 and 120 days) and one year for a year-long נזירות (two and four years).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the waiting times are not fixed numbers. They are built from the length of the person's own נזירות, because each shaving can happen only at the end of a full period.

phrases.english: And it was taught about it:
In what case are these words said?
With a short naziriteship,
phrases.notes: A short נזירות is the regular thirty-day kind.

phrases.english: but with a naziriteship of a year,
he eats sacrificial food after two years.
And he drinks wine and becomes impure for the dead
after four years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the 60 and 120 day figures from Step 1 to a short נזירות, and gives the matching figures for a year-long נזירות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a year-long נזירות, the doubtful נזיר eats קדשים after two years, and drinks wine and becomes טמא to the dead after four years.

steps.title: If the days counted, three years and thirty days would be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the days of צרעת counted toward נזירות, the ברייתא should have required only three years and thirty days, not four years.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the days count for him, then three years and thirty days should be enough for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge against רב חסדא. It does the math to show that the ברייתא's four years only makes sense if the days of צרעת do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the doubt, he waits one year before his צרעת shaving and another year before his second shaving. If those days counted, he would then need only thirty days of hair growth and one more pure year, which is about three years and thirty days. The ברייתא says four years, so the days of צרעת must not count.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind; you might think
They count for him; they go up toward his total
It should be enough for him

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that the days count for him
phrases.notes: He means the days he spent as a מצורע. This is the view of רב חסדא that the גמרא is attacking.

phrases.english: it should be enough for him
with three years and thirty days!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ סָלְקִין לֵיהּ יוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the four-year figure from the ברייתא in Step 2 to challenge רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the days of צרעת count toward נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the days counted, the total would be three years and thirty days. The ברייתא requires four years, so the days must not count.

steps.title: רב אשי brings a ברייתא about the days of confirmed צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes a ברייתא. It knows that days of טומאה do not count and asks for the source that days of confirmed צרעת do not count either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי raised another objection: I only know that days of טומאה do not count toward the total. How do I know that the days of his confirmed צרעת also do not count?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a second challenge against רב חסדא by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא asks a question, and the next steps show how it answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא takes it for granted that days of confirmed צרעת do not count. It only asks where we learn this from. That assumption alone already goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised a further objection
Days when the נזיר is impure from a dead body
The days when he is a confirmed מצורע
They count toward his total of נזירות days

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi raised a further objection:
I have only the days of impurity,
that they do not count for him toward the tally.
The days of his confirmed leprosy, from where?
phrases.notes: "Confirmed" means the כהן has declared him a definite מצורע, not just someone being watched to see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate challenge against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that the days of צרעת count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא assumes that days of confirmed צרעת do not count and only looks for the source.

steps.title: A first proof: comparing צרעת to טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a comparison. In both cases he shaves and brings a קרבן, so just as days of טומאה do not count, days of צרעת should not count either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: after days of טומאה he shaves and brings a קרבן, and after days of confirmed צרעת he also shaves and brings a קרבן. Just as days of טומאה do not count, days of צרעת should not count either.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries its first proof by comparing the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases share something: each one ends with shaving and bringing a קרבן. Based on that shared feature, the ברייתא wants to apply the טומאה rule (the days do not count) to צרעת as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical; a reasoned proof
He shaves and brings an offering

phrases.english: And it is logical:
days of impurity: he shaves and brings an offering,
and days of his confirmed leprosy: he shaves and brings an offering.
Just as his days of impurity
do not count for him toward the tally,
so too his days of confirmed leprosy
do not count for him toward the tally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: Days of confirmed צרעת do not count toward נזירות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to days of טומאה, since both end with shaving and a קרבן

steps.title: The comparison fails: טומאה cancels earlier days, צרעת does not
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is rejected. טומאה is stricter because it cancels the days he already kept, while צרעת does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can say this about days of טומאה, because they cancel the earlier days. But can you say it about days of confirmed צרעת, which do not cancel the earlier days?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down its own first proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה has an extra strictness that צרעת lacks: it wipes out the days he already counted. So the fact that days of טומאה do not count may come from that strictness, and we cannot carry the rule over to the milder case of צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: No. If you said it about this case (opens a rejection)
Cancels the earlier days

phrases.english: No. If you said this about his days of impurity,
which cancel the earlier days,
will you say it about his days of confirmed leprosy,
which do not cancel the earlier days?

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison to טומאה. The conclusion is still being sought.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: טומאה has a strictness (it cancels earlier days) that צרעת does not have.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a נזיר in a graveyard
steps.stepSummary: A נזיר who vowed in a graveyard can use his hair for the נזירות shaving, yet his days do not count. A מצורע's hair is not even fit for that shaving, so his days certainly do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say it is a קל וחומר: a נזיר in a graveyard, whose hair is fit for the נזירות shaving, does not get those days counted toward his total. Days of confirmed צרעת, when his hair is not fit for the נזירות shaving, should certainly not count!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא replaces its rejected comparison with a new, stronger proof that days of confirmed צרעת do not count. The ברייתא is not finished yet: it goes on to ask about ימי ספרו in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The graveyard case is milder, because his hair could still be used for the נזירות shaving, and even so his days do not count. During צרעת his hair is not fit for that shaving, so his days should not count all the more. The ברייתא therefore concludes that days of צרעת do not count, against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a milder case to a stricter one
A נזיר who took his vow in a graveyard, a טמא place
The shaving that a נזיר does as part of his נזירות
Is it not all the more so?

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves with a קל וחומר that days of confirmed צרעת do not count toward נזירות. This is a strong challenge to רב חסדא.

phrases.english: You can say: it is a kal vachomer:
If a nazir in a grave,
phrases.notes: This is someone who made his נזיר vow while standing in a טמא place like a graveyard.

phrases.english: whose hair is fit for the nazirite shaving,
does not have those days count for him toward the tally,
then his days of confirmed leprosy,
when his hair is not fit for the nazirite shaving,
phrases.notes: As a מצורע, he first has to do the צרעת shaving, so his hair cannot serve for the נזיר shaving.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison from Step 6 with a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: Days of confirmed צרעת do not count toward נזירות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a נזיר who vowed in a graveyard

steps.title: What about his days of counting toward purification?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says it has only proven that ימי חלוטו do not count, and asks for the source that ימי ספרו do not count either. It then begins a logical argument to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know this about his days of confirmed צרעת. How do I know it about his days of counting toward purification? It can be shown by logic:
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes the rule one step further and asks how we know that a מצורע's counting days also do not count toward his נזירות. With the words "ודין הוא" it is setting up a logical proof, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 proved only that the days of confirmed צרעת do not count. After he heals, he counts days toward purification and is no longer a confirmed מצורע, so this is a different stage. The ברייתא asks for a separate source for ימי ספרו and announces that it will derive it by reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: "I only have": so far the source teaches only this case
His days of counting: the days he counts after healing, before he is fully pure
"From where?": what is the source?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two stages. ימי חלוטו is while he is still sick and declared a מצורע. ימי ספרו comes after he is healed, while he is still finishing his purification.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether the whole time of צרעת, including recovery, is cut out of the נזירות.

phrases.english: And I have derived only his days of confirmed leprosy.
His days of counting, from where do I know they don't count?
phrases.notes: These are the days he counts after healing, before he becomes fully pure.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
phrases.notes: This opens a reasoning argument. The ברייתא lays it out on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא יְמֵי חִלּוּטוֹ. יְמֵי סְפָרוֹ, מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the conclusion of Step 7 (ימי חלוטו do not count) and asks for a source that also covers the next stage, ימי ספרו. It then begins setting up a logical proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a מצורע's counting days toward purification (ימי ספרו) also do not count toward his נזירות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not given on this amud. The ברייתא only announces "ודין הוא", and its reasoning continues on the next amud.
